messages.content: Write a self-contained fable of exactly 150 words about two parrots who disagree about sharing credit. Output no title or preamble. Include the final one-sentence moral in the 150-word total. Before responding, silently revise the draft until the entire response is between 140 and 170 words.

text: The mango tree held two parrots who had found the same ripe fruit. "I spotted it first," said Rio, puffing his green feathers. "But I flew faster," countered Kiki, shaking her crimson crest. Each insisted the discovery belonged to her alone—wait, to him alone. Rio claimed the finding; Kiki claimed the flight. They argued until sunset, each reciting their own version of the morning to any bird who would listen. The mango, unclaimed and uneaten, ripened past sweetness and dropped, rotting into the roots below. A tortoise passing by ate it happily and remarked, "While you two quarreled over whose achievement this was, I simply enjoyed the fruit." Rio and Kiki stared at the empty ground where their prize had been. Neither could remember exactly who had seen it first, or flown fastest, or mattered at all. The moral: credit shared is fruit enjoyed; credit hoarded feeds only strangers.
